# Symbolic equilibrium and stability analysis {#sec-symbolic-analysis}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Self-study**: not taught at the workshop, but complete and ready to use on your own.
:::

@sec-foundations asserted that $R_0 = \beta c/\gamma$ and that an epidemic grows
while $S/N > 1/R_0$. Both were derived on paper and then merely *evaluated* in
Julia. Every chapter since has simulated, fitted or optimised a model; none has
analysed one.

This appendix closes that gap with a computer algebra system. `Symbolics.jl`
manipulates expressions rather than numbers, so we can differentiate a vector
field into a Jacobian, evaluate it at an equilibrium, form a characteristic
polynomial, and read a stability condition off its coefficients — all in terms
of the parameters, valid for every parameter value at once rather than the one
we happened to simulate.

## Learning goals

You will:

- represent a model's vector field symbolically and obtain its Jacobian;
- locate the disease-free and endemic equilibria and verify them mechanically;
- apply the Routh--Hurwitz criteria to decide stability without computing roots;
- derive $R_0$ from a next-generation matrix and recover @sec-foundations' formula; and
- recognise where a CAS stops helping.

## Model assumptions and classification

The SIR model of @sec-ordinary-differential-equations is a poor vehicle for this
analysis, and it is worth saying why. Without demography every state with $I=0$
is an equilibrium, so there is a *line* of them rather than isolated points, the
Jacobian inherits a structural zero eigenvalue, and linear stability analysis
degenerates. The epidemic simply burns out; there is nothing to be endemic.

We therefore add **demography**: births at rate $\mu N$ into $S$, and a per-capita
death rate $\mu$ from every compartment, so the population size is constant at
$N$ but individuals turn over. This is a deliberate deviation from the course
baseline, and it is the minimum needed for an isolated endemic equilibrium to
exist. The model remains **deterministic, continuous-time, continuous-state and
population-level**.

## Equations

With $\kappa = \beta c/N$ the vector field is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot S &= \mu N - \beta c\,\frac{SI}{N} - \mu S,\\
\dot I &= \beta c\,\frac{SI}{N} - \gamma I - \mu I,\\
\dot R &= \gamma I - \mu R.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-a10-vector-field}

Setting $\dot I = 0$ gives either $I=0$ or $S = N(\gamma+\mu)/\beta c$. The first
is the **disease-free equilibrium** $(S,I,R) = (N,0,0)$. The second, substituted
into $\dot S = 0$, gives the **endemic equilibrium**

$$
S^\star = \frac{N(\gamma+\mu)}{\beta c},
\qquad
I^\star = \frac{\mu N\,(\beta c - \gamma - \mu)}{\beta c\,(\gamma+\mu)}.
$$ {#eq-a10-endemic}

Note that $I^\star > 0$ requires $\beta c > \gamma + \mu$. The endemic
equilibrium does not merely become unstable below that threshold — it leaves the
positive orthant and stops being a state at all.

**Local stability** of an equilibrium $x^\star$ is decided by the Jacobian
$J = \partial f/\partial x$ evaluated there: the equilibrium is locally
asymptotically stable when every eigenvalue of $J(x^\star)$ has negative real
part. Rather than computing roots, the **Routh--Hurwitz criteria** give
equivalent conditions on the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial. For
a quadratic $\lambda^2 + a_1\lambda + a_2$ they reduce to

$$
a_1 > 0 \quad\text{and}\quad a_2 > 0,
$$ {#eq-a10-rh-quadratic}

and for a cubic $\lambda^3 + a_1\lambda^2 + a_2\lambda + a_3$ to

$$
a_1 > 0,\qquad a_3 > 0,\qquad a_1 a_2 > a_3.
$$ {#eq-a10-rh-cubic}

This is why a CAS and Routh--Hurwitz suit each other: the coefficients are
polynomial in the parameters and a CAS produces them exactly, whereas the roots
of a cubic are unusable as symbolic expressions.

## Julia implementation

`@variables` introduces symbols. Nothing here is a number: `f` is an expression,
and `Symbolics.jacobian` differentiates it exactly.

```{julia}
#| label: code-a10-setup
using Symbolics
using OrdinaryDiffEq
using CairoMakie
using LinearAlgebra

@variables S I R λ
@variables βc γ μ N

f = [μ*N - βc*S*I/N - μ*S,
     βc*S*I/N - γ*I - μ*I,
     γ*I - μ*R]

J = Symbolics.jacobian(f, [S, I, R])
size(J)
```

### The disease-free equilibrium

Substituting $S=N$, $I=0$ leaves a Jacobian whose middle row carries the whole
threshold.

```{julia}
#| label: code-a10-dfe
J_dfe = Symbolics.simplify.(Symbolics.substitute.(J, (Dict(S => N, I => 0),)))
J_dfe
```

The characteristic polynomial factors without help, so the eigenvalues can be
read off directly. Note the identity matrix is written out: `@variables S I R`
has bound `I` to the infectious class, shadowing `LinearAlgebra.I`, which is a
collision worth knowing about in epidemic modelling.

```{julia}
#| label: code-a10-charpoly
identity₃ = [1 0 0; 0 1 0; 0 0 1]   # `I` is the infectious class here, not LinearAlgebra.I
characteristic = Symbolics.simplify(Symbolics.det(J_dfe - λ*identity₃))
characteristic
```

Two eigenvalues are $-\mu$ and the third is $\beta c - \gamma - \mu$. The
disease-free equilibrium is therefore stable exactly when
$\beta c < \gamma + \mu$ — the threshold of @sec-foundations, now derived rather
than asserted, and corrected for the fact that infectives can also die.

### $R_0$ from a next-generation matrix

Splitting the infected subsystem into new infections $F$ and transitions out $V$
gives $R_0 = \rho(FV^{-1})$. Here the infected subsystem is one-dimensional, so
the spectral radius is the single entry.

```{julia}
#| label: code-a10-ngm
F = [βc*S/N]
V = [γ + μ]
R₀_expression = Symbolics.simplify(Symbolics.substitute(F[1] / V[1], Dict(S => N)))
R₀_expression
```

As $\mu \to 0$ this collapses to $\beta c/\gamma$, exactly @sec-foundations'
formula. The demographic correction is the chance of dying before recovering.

### Verifying the endemic equilibrium

`symbolic_solve` cannot solve @eq-a10-vector-field, for reasons taken up in the
limitations below. It does not need to: substituting @eq-a10-endemic into the
vector field and simplifying is a complete proof that it *is* an equilibrium.

```{julia}
#| label: code-a10-endemic-check
S_star = N*(γ + μ)/βc
I_star = μ*N*(βc - γ - μ)/(βc*(γ + μ))
residual = Symbolics.simplify.(
    Symbolics.substitute.(f[1:2], (Dict(S => S_star, I => I_star),)); expand = true)
residual
```

Both residuals are identically zero, for every parameter value.

### Stability of the endemic equilibrium

$R$ appears in no other equation and $N$ is constant, so the dynamics reduce to
$(S,I)$ and the characteristic polynomial is a quadratic. Routh--Hurwitz for a
quadratic, @eq-a10-rh-quadratic, is the familiar pair: negative trace and
positive determinant.

```{julia}
#| label: code-a10-endemic-stability
J₂ = Symbolics.jacobian(f[1:2], [S, I])
J₂_endemic = Symbolics.simplify.(
    Symbolics.substitute.(J₂, (Dict(S => S_star, I => I_star),)); expand = true)

trace_endemic = Symbolics.simplify(J₂_endemic[1, 1] + J₂_endemic[2, 2]; expand = true)
det_endemic = Symbolics.simplify(
    J₂_endemic[1, 1]*J₂_endemic[2, 2] - J₂_endemic[1, 2]*J₂_endemic[2, 1]; expand = true)
(trace = trace_endemic, determinant = det_endemic)
```

The trace is negative and the determinant is positive precisely when
$\beta c > \gamma + \mu$ — the same threshold. So the two equilibria exchange
stability at $R_0 = 1$: below it the disease-free state is stable and the
endemic state is not positive; above it the endemic state exists and is stable.

## Validation

Symbolic results are worth little until checked against the numerics the rest of
the course uses. Three independent checks follow.

```{julia}
#| label: code-a10-validation
parameter_values = Dict(βc => 0.5, γ => 0.25, μ => 0.01, N => 1000.0)
substitute_value(expr) = Float64(Symbolics.value(
    Symbolics.substitute(expr, parameter_values)))

S_star_numeric = substitute_value(S_star)
I_star_numeric = substitute_value(I_star)
R₀_numeric = substitute_value(R₀_expression)

function sir_demography!(du, u, p, t)
    βc_, γ_, μ_, N_ = p
    du[1] = μ_*N_ - βc_*u[1]*u[2]/N_ - μ_*u[1]
    du[2] = βc_*u[1]*u[2]/N_ - γ_*u[2] - μ_*u[2]
    du[3] = γ_*u[2] - μ_*u[3]
end

long_run = solve(
    ODEProblem(sir_demography!, [990.0, 10.0, 0.0], (0.0, 4000.0),
               (0.5, 0.25, 0.01, 1000.0)),
    Tsit5(); abstol = 1e-10, reltol = 1e-10)

numerical_S, numerical_I = long_run.u[end][1], long_run.u[end][2]
J_numeric = [substitute_value(J₂_endemic[i, j]) for i in 1:2, j in 1:2]

(R₀ = round(R₀_numeric; digits = 4),
 S_star_symbolic = round(S_star_numeric; digits = 4),
 S_star_simulated = round(numerical_S; digits = 4),
 I_star_symbolic = round(I_star_numeric; digits = 4),
 I_star_simulated = round(numerical_I; digits = 4),
 eigenvalues = round.(eigvals(J_numeric); digits = 5),
 routh_hurwitz_satisfied = substitute_value(trace_endemic) < 0 &&
                           substitute_value(det_endemic) > 0)
```

The simulated equilibrium matches @eq-a10-endemic, the numerically computed
eigenvalues have negative real parts, and the Routh--Hurwitz verdict agrees with
them. The eigenvalues being complex is itself informative: the approach to the
endemic state is oscillatory, which is the damped epidemic cycling seen in
childhood-infection data.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-a10-threshold
#| fig-cap: "Endemic prevalence against the transmission parameter. The symbolic expression for $I^\\star$ (line) against long-run simulation (points), with the threshold $\\beta c = \\gamma + \\mu$ marked. Below it the endemic equilibrium is not positive and the disease-free state is stable."
βc_grid = collect(0.20:0.02:0.80)
symbolic_prevalence = [max(substitute_value(
    Symbolics.substitute(I_star, Dict(βc => value))), 0.0) for value in βc_grid]
simulated_prevalence = map(βc_grid) do value
    solution = solve(
        ODEProblem(sir_demography!, [990.0, 10.0, 0.0], (0.0, 6000.0),
                   (value, 0.25, 0.01, 1000.0)),
        Tsit5(); abstol = 1e-10, reltol = 1e-10)
    max(solution.u[end][2], 0.0)
end

figure = Figure(size = (720, 380))
axis = Axis(figure[1, 1], xlabel = "βc", ylabel = "Endemic infectious I*")
lines!(axis, βc_grid, symbolic_prevalence; color = :firebrick, linewidth = 2,
       label = "Symbolic I*")
scatter!(axis, βc_grid, simulated_prevalence; color = :grey25, markersize = 7,
         label = "Long-run simulation")
vlines!(axis, [0.26]; color = :steelblue, linestyle = :dash,
        label = "Threshold βc = γ + μ")
axislegend(axis; position = :lt, framevisible = false)
figure
```

## Interpretation and limitations

A CAS is not an oracle that solves models. It is a tool that performs mechanical
algebra without slips, and its value here is that every result holds for all
parameter values at once, where a simulation speaks only about the parameters it
was given.

The boundaries are real. `Symbolics.symbolic_solve` cannot solve
@eq-a10-vector-field for its equilibria: the system is *rational* rather than
polynomial because of the division by $N$, and the polynomial-solving backends
require a polynomial ideal. Clearing denominators would make it polynomial, but
deciding that this is legitimate — that $N \neq 0$, that no root is introduced —
is a modelling judgement the CAS will not make for you. Hence the pattern used
above: derive the equilibrium by hand, and let the CAS *verify* it, which it does
completely.

Expression swell is the other limit. The quadratic here is readable; a cubic
from an SEIR model is manageable through Routh--Hurwitz but not through its
roots; beyond four compartments symbolic characteristic polynomials become
unusable and numerical continuation is the practical route. Everything here is
also strictly *local*: linearisation says what happens near an equilibrium and
nothing about the basin of attraction or about behaviour far from it.

## Exercises

### Exercise 1 {#a10-ex1}

Add an exposed class to @eq-a10-vector-field, with $E$ entering at rate
$\beta c SI/N$ and leaving to $I$ at rate $\sigma$, all classes still subject to
the death rate $\mu$. Form the Jacobian at the disease-free equilibrium
symbolically, obtain the characteristic polynomial of the $2\times2$ infected
subsystem, and apply the Routh--Hurwitz conditions to derive the threshold. Show
that the resulting $R_0$ is
$\beta c\,\sigma / \bigl((\sigma+\mu)(\gamma+\mu)\bigr)$, and explain the factor
$\sigma/(\sigma+\mu)$ epidemiologically.

### Exercise 2 {#a10-ex2}

Replace demography with waning immunity: no births or deaths, but $R \to S$ at
rate $\omega$. Derive the endemic equilibrium of the resulting SIRS model, verify
it symbolically by substitution, and use the trace and determinant of the reduced
$2\times2$ Jacobian to determine when the approach to it is oscillatory rather
than monotone. Confirm your condition by simulating one parameter set either side
of it.
